scenario: [LTIM.4.2.3] with [LNUL.4.1]: a `null` operand of `Date` arithmetic yields `null`, and raises no fault. `due`, `step` and `other` are nullable. Rule `shifted` fires where `(v.due + v.step) is null` and rule `apart` where `(v.due - v.other) is null`; rule `handler` logs any ComputationError. Visit 1 has no `due`; Visit 2 has a `due` and neither of the others; Visit 3 has all three, whole days, so neither rule fires for it. Messages, rule then assertion order: `shifted 1`, `shifted 2`, `apart 1`, `apart 2`, and no fault. A builtin that faulted on a null operand would log no `shifted` or `apart` line and a ComputationError handler line instead. PATH PINNED: the null arm of FN_DATE_ADD_DURATION and FN_DATE_DIFF in libds (`rete/adapters.c`) and Mercury (`ds.eval`), ahead of their kind checks.
rules_ds:
schema Visit scope logical:
    id: Int key
    due: Date? mutable
    step: Duration? mutable
    other: Date? mutable

rule shifted:
    Visit v where (v.due + v.step) is null
->
    log info "shifted {v.id}"

rule apart:
    Visit v where (v.due - v.other) is null
->
    log info "apart {v.id}"

rule handler:
    ComputationError e
->
    log critical "{e.kind} {e.rule}"
